主要内容: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. closed a $14 billion global infrastructure fund on July 12, 2016, under Rule 12g3-2(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The fund's closure was confirmed by Brian D. Lawson, Chief Financial Officer of Brookfield Asset Management Inc. Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III raised $14 billion in equity commitments, bringing total funds raised in the past 18 months to $27 billion. This includes $9 billion for Brookfield Strategic Real Estate Partners II and $4 billion for Brookfield Capital Partners IV. Brookfield committed $4 billion to the Fund, which will be funded through Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. and Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. Sam Pollock, head of Brookfield’s infrastructure business, stated that the fundraise demonstrates growing demand for infrastructure investing as investors increase allocations to real assets. Brookfield has committed to invest over $3 billion in assets consistent with its investment strategy, including U.S. hydroelectric facilities, Brazilian electricity transmission projects, a Colombian power generation company, Peruvian toll roads, and a U.S. water infrastructure project developer. Securities explicitly mentioned in the source include BAM.
